text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — saw a perf regression on nightly after the driver bump. 99p latency jumped ~18% for seqlen 2-8. Traces show requests landing on the generic kernel path instead of arch-optimized kernels.

Jess: ugh. which model/version + can you paste a flame/trace? :eyes:

Sam: model=v1.14.2 (gpt-ish family), driver=driver-2024-11-03. snippet from debug logs: 
```
[2024-11-04T03:12:11Z] kernel_selector: picked kernel=generic_nhwc_v2 for model=gpt-ish@v1.14.2 seqlen=4 cpu=amd-epyc-rome flags=[avx2=false, amx=false]
[2024-11-04T03:12:11Z] kvcache: miss key=cache_v2:session:abc123:kernelmeta:generic_nhwc_v2
```
This used to pick `kern_x86_avx2_v1` on the same host.

Ritesh: sounds like kernel metadata changed shape after the driver update -> selector fallback. That also means KV keys that encoded kernel_tag no longer match, so KV miss -> full recompute and slower path.

Kai: agreed. Two levers: 1) make kernel selection deterministic w/ backward compat tags, 2) change cache key schema to be robust when selector metadata changes. We should do both.

Jess: propose immediate mitigation: roll driver back on canary hosts, and add a compatibility layer that maps old kernel tags to new ones (short term). Sam can run a quick canary revert?

Sam: I can revert the driver on the nightly pool now (will do canary 3 hosts). scheduling revert at 03:30 UTC.

Ritesh: for longer term, here's the keying plan I sketched: keys = join(":", [prefix, model_hash, model_version, kernel_family, kernel_semver, selector_config_hash, salt_v])
- `kernel_family` groups compatible kernels (e.g., x86-avx2)
- `kernel_semver` increments when internal ABI changes
- `selector_config_hash` is a stable hash of the selector policy (seqlen bins, arch rules)
- `salt_v` is a monotonic migration tag we can bump to invalidate old keys safely

Kai: that looks solid. Also we need persistence migration steps: write-through new keys while keeping old keys readable for X days; background job that backfills new keys when old hits occur; a prune job to remove old keys after TTL.

Jess: agree — add an explicit `migration_state` flag in metadata so tools know whether to backfill or only read. set default TTL=7d for backfilled keys.

Sam: do we need immediate invalidation on model change/driver upgrade? I worry about capacity spike from mass backfills.

Ritesh: don't mass invalidate. Use staged invalidation: on driver upgrade we: 
1) bump `salt_v` on a tiny canary subset (5%)
2) monitor hit rate and token-cost bump
3) if safe, gradually increase to 25%, 50%, 100% over 48h.
This avoids thundering herd.

Kai: monitoring hooks required: KV hit rate, per-seqlen 50/90/99p latency, token throughput, and write amplification. Add alerts if KV hit rate drops >15% and 99p latency up >10%.

Jess: can we add a quick perf regression test in CI that simulates seqlen distribution and validates selector picks? If we catch selector changes earlier, fewer surprises.

Sam: I'll add a smoke test that runs selector with sampled host features and sequence buckets (2,4,8,16,64) and asserts preferred kernel families for each. Put it in infra-tests. PR incoming.

Ritesh: I'll start the cache-migration util: `kv-migrate --dry-run --from-salt v0 --to-salt v1 --sample 10000` that outputs expected backfill/writes. Also will add tests that ensure old keys still read when `migration_state=read-only`.

Jess: owner list: Sam (rollback & smoke test), Ritesh (kv key schema + migration tool), Kai (rollout policy + alerts), Ops (monitor canary). Add tickets: INFRA-2145 (key schema), RUNTIME-3310 (selector CI), DEPLOY-998 (driver rollback procedure).

deploy-bot: deploy plan: revert driver on canary hosts scheduled at 2024-11-04T03:30Z — ticket DEPLOY-998 linked.

Sam: revert done on 3 hosts, initial metrics look good; 99p back to baseline. Will start the selector smoke test PR after breakfast.

Kai: timeline for key schema rollout? Ritesh: plan is: design -> dev tests (48h) -> canary migrate (1%) -> staged ramp 1/24/48h -> full. Expect ~5 working days to reach full deployment if no surprises.

Jess: cool. let's document the runbook steps in the ops playbook (links when PRs land). also add a short note for oncall: if you see seqlen-2..8 99p regression after driver bump, check kernel_selector logs + kv hit rate and escalate to eng-runtime.

Sam: TL;DR actions tracked: Sam=rollback + selector-smoke PR; Ritesh=key-schema + kv-migrate tool; Kai=rollout policy + alerts; Jess=document.

Kai: thanks everyone. :thumbsup: we avoided a larger outage.

Jess: filing the three tickets now. will post links here.
